sections.heading: C — Pedestrian Safety
sections.markdown:
## C — Pedestrian Safety

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
Walkers obey traffic signals unless pedestrian signals redirect them, waiting on curbs rather than streets for green or WALK phases [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
Walkers never cross mid-block between intersections, keep right inside crosswalks where possible, and look both ways before crossing and before emerging from behind parked cars [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
Walkers take sidewalks where they exist, otherwise walk left facing traffic and step off pavement for approaching cars [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
Walkers crossing outside intersection crosswalks or bypassing provided tunnels and overpasses yield to every vehicle [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A01
White canes belong solely to blind, partially blind, or disabled walkers on public roads, and nobody stands in roads seeking rides, contributions, or business except locally authorized charitable solicitors [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A01
Walkers never dart into vehicle paths, wear white or light clothes with lights or reflectors at night, step carefully from buses and streetcars, enter and leave cars curbside, avoid walking while drinking since alcohol feeds walker crashes, and heed local bans on business-district and designated-highway crossings outside crosswalks [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A01
Drivers spotting crossing or attempting walkers slow, sound horns when needed, and ready full stops [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A01
Drivers heed assistance animals and white canes marking blind, partially blind, or disabled walkers, take every precaution against harming crossing or attempting walkers, and stop fully whenever only stopping avoids injury or danger [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A01
Drivers watch for blind individuals at bus stops, intersections, business districts, and schools for the blind [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A01
Drivers always pay special attention to persons on foot [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0067]
